title: Child Rights
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Handle gently: some learners may be living with abuse. Give Childline 116 and the name of a trusted teacher. No learner shares personal experiences in class; any disclosure is followed up privately by the teacher under the school's safeguarding policy.

skills.key_step: The child names forms of child abuse (beating that injures, neglect, child labour, early marriage, FGM, sexual abuse, trafficking) and tells light chores from child labour.

floor.question: Name one right of a child.
floor.answer: any of: education, food, shelter, protection, health care, play

representations: story cards of safe and unsafe situations
a list of trusted adults in school
steps: Ask whether a child's right is being broken.
Name the form of abuse if it is.
Name who the child can tell.
contexts: a girl kept home to sell at the market every school day
a boy working long hours in a quarry
a child left alone without food

board.do: Write two sentences: "Ali helps wash the dishes." and "Ali breaks stones at a quarry all day instead of going to school."
Wait for the second and the reason.

misconceptions.ask: A teacher beats a learner until he is hurt. Is this child abuse?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: does discipline teach with care or hurt? Discuss other ways, such as talking and fair consequences.
Sort examples by: safe, short, does not stop school, does not harm.

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is child abuse?
misconceptions.repair: List six forms and ask: how does each harm the child?

misconceptions.ask: Can a child be abused by someone they know?
misconceptions.repair: Say plainly that anyone who hurts a child is wrong, whoever they are, and the child should tell a trusted adult.

checks.question: A girl of 13 is married off. Which form of abuse is this?
Is helping to sweep the house child labour?
checks.answer: No: it is a light chore

skills.key_step: The child gives causes of child abuse (poverty, ignorance, harmful customs, greed, drugs and alcohol) and says it is never the child's fault.

floor.question: Name one form of child abuse.
floor.answer: any form such as child labour

representations: a story with the cause hidden
steps: Ask what led the adult to do it.
Say the child is not to blame.
contexts: a family sending a child to work because there is no money
an adult drinking and hitting a child

board.do: Write: "A child was sent to work in a house in town because the family had no money."
Write poverty, then add: it is not the child's fault.

misconceptions.ask: Why was a child abused by an adult?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: can anything a child does make it right for an adult to hurt him or her?

listen_for: It is fine if it is a tradition
misconceptions.ask: Some say a harmful custom is fine because it is old. What is right?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss that culture changes, and that keeping children safe is also a tradition.

misconceptions.ask: Does child abuse happen only in poor homes?
misconceptions.repair: List several causes together: drugs, harmful customs, greed, ignorance.

misconceptions.ask: A drunk adult hit a child. Is the adult to blame?
misconceptions.repair: Separate cause from blame: alcohol can lead to it, the adult still chose to drink and to hit.

checks.question: Give two causes of child abuse.
checks.answer: any two of: poverty, ignorance, harmful customs, greed, drugs and alcohol, war

checks.question: A learner says a child was beaten because she was naughty, so it was her fault. Is this right?
checks.answer: No: abuse is never the child's fault

skills.key_step: The child names effects of abuse (injury, fear, sadness, dropping out, poor health) and says a hurt child tells a trusted adult or calls Childline 116.

floor.question: Is beating a child until they are hurt a form of abuse?

representations: a story of a child who got help
steps: Name the effect on the body.
Name the effect on feelings and school.
contexts: a girl who drops out after early marriage
a boy who is afraid to go home
a friend who tells you a secret about being hurt

board.do: Draw a sad face and a schoolbag.

board.say: What can happen to a child's schooling after abuse?

board.do: Wait for dropping out or poor marks.
Write "tell a trusted adult or call 116".

misconceptions.ask: What can child abuse do to a child?
misconceptions.repair: List ways a bad experience at school changes how a learner feels.

misconceptions.ask: A friend tells you an adult is hurting him. What should you do?
misconceptions.repair: Make a list of the adults who keep children safe and practise saying "I need to tell you something".

misconceptions.ask: A child's bruise has healed. Can the child still be hurt by the abuse?
misconceptions.repair: Talk about how a child might feel afraid or sad long after, using a story character.

misconceptions.ask: A child is being hurt. Who can help?
misconceptions.repair: Name the helpers: a teacher, a parent, a chief, a nurse, Childline 116. Practise what to say.

checks.question: Give one effect of child abuse.
checks.answer: any of: injury, fear, sadness, dropping out of school, poor health

checks.question: Your friend tells you someone is hurting her and asks you to keep it secret. What should you do?
checks.answer: Tell a trusted adult such as a teacher
